sources.says: Australia (30 June 2026), Japan (07 August 2026), New Zealand (06 July 2026), Singapore (02 July 2026), Taiwan (20 August 2026) and the Republic of Korea (04 June 2026) are all "NA": "the territory does not have the indicated tax".

claims.claim: A temporary resident (temporary visa, no Australian-resident spouse) is taxed only on Australian income and gains on Australian real property, so US dividends, interest and share gains go untaxed while the visa lasts

sources.name: PwC: Australia, residence
sources.says: Last reviewed 12 October 2026. A temporary resident is broadly an individual who "holds a temporary visa granted under the Migration Act 1958", is not an Australian resident under the Social Security Act and "does not have an Australian spouse"; "A temporary resident will be exempt from Australian tax on foreign source income."

sources.name: PwC: Australia, income determination
sources.says: Reviewed October 2026. For assets held at least 12 months, disposals up to 30 June 2027 include 50% of the nominal gain; from 1 July 2027 the discount is replaced by cost base indexation with a minimum 30% tax on post-1 July 2027 gains. Non-residents get no discount on gains accrued after 7:30 pm AEST on 8 May 2012. Temporary residents are excluded from the rule taxing residents on gains from assets wherever located, and are generally exempt on foreign-source income.

claims.claim: A permanent resident is taxed on worldwide income at up to 45% plus the 2% Medicare levy

sources.name: PwC: Australia, taxes on personal income
sources.says: 2026/27 resident rates: 45% over AUD 190,000; "The above tables do not include the Medicare levy of an additional 2% of taxable income"; "A resident individual is subject to Australian income tax on a worldwide basis", except "certain foreign income and gains of temporary residents".

claims.claim: Half of a gain on assets held over a year is taxed until June 2027, when indexation and a 30% minimum tax replace the discount, as proposed in the 2026 budget

sources.name: KPMG TaxNewsFlash: Australia, CGT legislation passes Parliament with amendments
sources.says: Dated June 26, 2026. Parliament passed the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Bill 2026, which "replaces the 50% CGT discount for individuals, trusts and partnerships with cost base indexation" and introduces a 30% minimum tax, "effective for all capital gains accruing on and after July 1, 2027".

sources.name: PwC: Australia, income determination
sources.says: Reviewed October 2026. For assets held at least 12 months, disposals up to 30 June 2027 include 50% of the nominal gain; from 1 July 2027 the discount is replaced by cost base indexation with a minimum 30% tax on post-1 July 2027 gains. Non-residents get no discount on gains accrued after 7:30 pm AEST on 8 May 2012. Temporary residents are excluded from the rule taxing residents on gains from assets wherever located, and are generally exempt on foreign-source income.

also: sources: replaced BDO's budget page with KPMG's note on the law's passage
claims.note: The 50% discount to June 2027 and the replacement are confirmed; what was wrong is "proposed": the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Bill 2026 passed Parliament on 26 June 2026. Tax scores unchanged (4), which rest on the temporary-resident exemption.

claims.claim: When an Australian resident dies leaving shares or other non-Australian-property assets to a non-resident heir, CGT event K3 taxes the unrealised gain in the final return as if sold

sources.name: Atlas Wealth: deceased estates with overseas connections
sources.says: Dated February 17, 2026. CGT event K3 applies where "A resident estate transfers an asset (e.g. property, shares) to a non-resident beneficiary" and the gain "would not otherwise be taxed in Australia"; the tax is payable by the estate.

sources.name: Bristax: CGT event K3
sources.says: Undated. K3 applies when the beneficiary is "A foreign resident" (or an exempt entity or complying super fund), the deceased was a tax resident and the asset is not taxable Australian property; "The trustee of the deceased estate must include any net capital gain in the date of death tax return."

claims.note: The ATO's CGT guide page on deceased estates (https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/capital-gains-tax-guide-2026/about-capital-gains-tax/deceased-estates) returned HTTP 403, so this rests on two secondary pages; Bristax names the date-of-death return.
claims.modelMismatch: localTaxes.ts has no Australia entry, so no tax at death is modelled. A permanent resident who leaves shares to US-resident children triggers CGT event K3 on the unrealised gain in the date-of-death return (marginal rates up to 45% + 2% Medicare levy, with the 50% discount on gains accrued to June 2027 and indexation plus a 30% minimum tax after).

claims.claim: A US estate and gift tax treaty exists

sources.name: IRS: Estate & gift tax treaties (international)
sources.says: All 13 countries are in the table (see us-estate-treaty-list). Estate & Gift: Australia, Austria, France, Germany, Japan, United Kingdom. Estate only: Greece, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, South Africa, Switzerland, and Canada by Article XXIX B of the income tax treaty.

claims.note: Wording: "the US–Australia estate and gift tax treaty applies".

claims.claim: The $15M US estate exemption (2026) applies to a US citizen living here as anywhere

sources.name: IRS: What's new, estate and gift tax
sources.says: The table "Basic exclusion amount for year of death" has the row 2026: $15,000,000 (2025: $13,990,000). The page says the Working Families Tax Cuts, Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, "amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026". Page last reviewed or updated 03-Nov-2026.

sources.name: IRS: Some nonresidents with U.S. assets must file estate tax returns
sources.says: "U.S. citizens are subject to U.S. estate taxation with respect to their worldwide assets"; Form 706 is required when worldwide assets plus adjusted taxable gifts exceed the basic exclusion amount in effect on the date of death. By contrast a nonresident who is not a citizen files when US-situated assets exceed $60,000. Page last reviewed or updated 27-Jun-2026.

claims.note: Wording: "the $15M US exemption (2026) applies as anywhere".

claims.claim: The Investor Retirement (405) and Retirement (410) visas are closed to new applicants; existing holders can renew

sources.name: NSW Government: Investor Retirement visa (subclass 405)
sources.says: Undated state government page. "This visa is closed to new applicants." Only "an existing Investor Retirement visa (subclass 405) holder" may apply.

sources.name: Widen: retire to Australia, visa options
sources.says: "Reviewed October 2026". Subclass 410 "closed to new applicants in 2005" and 405 in 2018; holders "can continue to apply for further visas in the same subclass". The Business Innovation and Investment Program "closed to new applications in July 2024 with no replacement for investors". The Sponsored Parent (Temporary) 870 allows "three or five years at a time, up to a total of ten years", "no Medicare and a requirement to hold health insurance"; the 143 queue "currently runs many years". Visitor stays "of up to 12 months" with no "more than 12 months in Australia in any 18-month period".
